as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Iran source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read on the cited page in this session. All ten come from one source, the U.S. EIA country analysis brief last updated 2024-10-10, so vintages are 2022 to early 2024 and predate the June 2025 and 2026 conflicts: they describe the system before those events and say nothing about its present state. Several are EIA estimates and are labelled so. Iranian official sites (Ministry of Petroleum, Ministry of Energy, Tavanir, Statistical Center of Iran) could not be read on this date, OPEC, IEA and the Energy Institute refused scripted access, and Iran has submitted no JODI-Oil data since July 2018, so no figure is taken from any of them. National installed generating capacity was not read on any page and is deliberately absent. See docs/countries/IR_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

significance: Natural gas made up 55.7% of Iran's primary energy production in 2022 and petroleum and other liquids 43.4% (EIA).
Natural gas supplied 67.6% of Iran's primary energy consumption and 85.2% of its electricity generation in 2022 (EIA).
Iran produced 9.4 trillion cubic feet of dry natural gas in 2023 and consumed 8.9 trillion cubic feet (EIA).
Iran produced 4.0 million barrels per day of petroleum and other liquids in 2023, of which almost 2.9 million barrels per day was crude oil (EIA).
EIA estimated Iran's proved natural gas reserves at 1,200 trillion cubic feet as of December 2023.
